verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Hyderabad API units with clean USFDA records and contracted offtake; avoid single-customer, high-leverage capex borrowers until unit-level cash flow is verified.
title: Hyderabad API / bulk drugs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**An API unit converts solvents, intermediates and imported starting materials into regulated-market bulk drugs, and cash comes back only after a customer audit, a stability batch and a repeat order.** Value sits in the DMF/CEP file and the USFDA-clean plant, not in the reactor. Pricing power is thin on commodity molecules and real only where you are the qualified second source. The working-capital cycle is long: a CARErating report on an API maker put the cycle at around 185 days, driven by raw-material inventory holding [9]. So when a proposal lands, check the inventory and receivables days against that 185-day marker; if receivables stretch past it, ask which customer and which molecule. ## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is strong but the national production signal is negative, and that gap is where bad loans hide.** Telangana GST collections ran +13.8% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and state electricity demand +15.7% against India +9.5% [D]. Yet India-wide pharma output is -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY, a gap of +23.7 pp [D]. **Credit is running far ahead of output, so the risk is a borrower funding inventory that is not moving.** On the ground, Granules India's Gagillapur finished-dosage site closed a USFDA inspection on 30 October 2026 with a Form FDA 483 carrying eleven observations, none on data integrity or cross-contamination [1]. That is a site-level quality signal, not a sector verdict, but it tells you audits are live and remediation spend is real. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][5], and RPG Life Sciences is targeting 25% API growth [7]. **Avoid the single-customer, single-molecule converter and any borrower whose only collateral story is a plant under a warning letter.** Hyderabad's partnering summit on 2-3 November 2026 [2][3] is a useful place to meet contract-manufacturing buyers, but a conference badge is not an order book. ## How to grow safely
**Structure against the audit cycle, not the sales projection.** Take monthly stock and debtor statements, quarterly GMP/audit status, and a covenant that any new USFDA observation above a stated count triggers a review. Ask for the customer-wise order book and the DMF/CEP list at sanction; collect from customer where the file status is unclear. **Cap exposure to greenfield reactor capex; fund only debottlenecking backed by a signed offtake.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch inventory days crossing the 185-day marker [9], a gearing push above 2 times on a large capex [8], and any revenue decline near 10% [8].** A warning letter or repeat 483 at the borrower's own site is an immediate stop-and-review.
watch: Inventory days above 185 [9] -> ask for molecule-wise ageing and freeze fresh limits
New 483 or warning letter at borrower site -> stop disbursement, review remediation cost
Gearing above 2 times with large capex [8] -> reprice or seek promoter infusion
Decline near 10% [8] -> shift to cash-flow-based limits
